subject: Quantara: production tail-latency & throughput throttle — escalation
messages:
From: Katy Zhang <katy@quantaralabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: support@quantaralabs.com
Date: 2026-07-13T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Production: sharp increase in tail latency and 429s since 09:00 PT

Hi Stephanie —

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 95th/99th tail latency at ~09:00 PT this morning. End users are experiencing intermittent 5–7s responses and a rising error rate (mostly 429 / upstream-timeout). Overall throughput appears capped even though request arrival is steady. This is impacting query-heavy workflows for our analytics customers.

Attached are a small sample of requests and our client-side timing. Can your team triage urgently? We’re pausing a few non-critical jobs but the problem persists.

Katy
Katy Zhang
Head of Platform — Quantara Labs
katy@quantaralabs.com

Attachments: quantara_client_request_samples.json (json)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Katy Zhang <katy@quantaralabs.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, support@quantaralabs.com
Date: 2026-07-13T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sharp increase in tail latency and 429s since 09:00 PT

Katy — thanks for the quick heads-up and the sample payloads. We’re escalating immediately.

Quick notes / asked actions:
- Dylan (SRE) & Markus (Serving) are on the call to triage traces and routing.
- Can you attach the full trace bundle (client traces + server request ids) when available?
- We’ll look at concurrency caps on your Dedicated pool, backpressure behavior, and any sudden kernel/quantization faults.

Temporary mitigations we’ll evaluate in parallel:
1) Route a small % of traffic to a lighter hosted variant (lower context, smaller model) to reduce KV/cache pressure.
2) Increase concurrency cap for Quantara’s pool for the next 2 hours to validate whether queueing is the root cause.
3) Toggle prefix/KV cache TTLs if we see repeated prefixes causing hot-shard effects.

I’ll keep you posted every 30 minutes. If we confirm customer impact beyond the committed SLA window we’ll start a credit discussion (Tom — I’ll loop you into the credit thread once we have firm numbers).

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Katy Zhang <katy@quantaralabs.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, support@quantaralabs.com
Date: 2026-07-13T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sharp increase in tail latency and 429s since 09:00 PT

We pulled a live trace bundle and I’ve uploaded a trimmed version to the shared drive (link below). Initial observations:
- Strong evidence of queueing at the dedicated replica layer: per-replica concurrency is hitting the configured cap (16 concurrent inference slots) and requests pile in the request queue.
- There are multiple long-running tokens caused by repeated large-batch requests from Quantara between 09:05–09:18 that push KV cache thrash.
- Backpressure is occurring at the admission layer, and our fallback policy is currently conservative (it preserves strict SLOs but increases 429s when the queue backs up).

Immediate steps taken (09:30–09:40):
- Temporarily raised per-replica concurrency to 24 for Quantara’s dedicated pool (soft cap; will revert if we see OOMs).
- Increased short-lived cache TTLs to reduce repeated cache misses.
- Enabled 5% traffic route to hosted smaller-quantized model.

I attached a server-side trace archive: redwood_trace_log_20260713.zip (contains request ids, per-replica metrics and kernel fallback events).

Dylan

Shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/share/quantara-trace-20260713
Attachments: redwood_trace_log_20260713.zip (zip)
From: Tom Ellis <tom@quantaralabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: support@quantaralabs.com, laura@quantara.com
Date: 2026-07-13T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sharp increase in tail latency and 429s since 09:00 PT

Thanks for the quick actions. Two comments from our side:
1) Quantara’s workload is bursty with periodic heavy analytic batches; we’ve always relied on the dedicated pool guarantees. Raising the per-replica concurrency reduces 429s but it looks like token-level CPU is spiking and some kernels fall back to slower paths when concurrency is >20.
2) Our customers started to complain; we need a remediation timeline and confirmation on credits for the period where uptime/latency violated the SLA (last 45 minutes).

FW: note from our ops slack (pasted):
> On Tue Jul 13 09:12:34 PDT, customer-alerts: Quantara jobs failing intermittently, engineering is seeing 429s. This is materially impacting scheduled analytics runs.

Can you confirm whether the root cause is: (A) queueing from strict concurrency caps, (B) KV cache thrashing from large batch sizes, or (C) a combination? We need clear public-facing guidance for our customers.

Tom
Tom Ellis
VP Engineering — Quantara Labs

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, Katy Zhang <katy@quantaralabs.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: Quantara production impact — exec summary & recommended authorizations

Laura / Sean —

Summary (so you can brief Execs):
- Impact: Quantara Labs observed elevated p95/p99 latency and increased 429s between 09:05–09:50 PT causing customer-facing failures for analytics runs.
- Root cause (prelim): Queueing at per-replica concurrency cap combined with KV cache thrashing from large batch patterns. Evidence: per-replica concurrency saturations + repeated cache-miss spikes (see trace).
- Measures already taken: temporary concurrency increase (16 -> 24), 5% traffic diversion to hosted lightweight model, cache TTL adjustments.

Requested approvals:
1) Short-term committed burst capacity for Quantara’s dedicated pool for the next 24 hours (estimate cost impact: $3.6k).
2) Approve a one-off customer credit if SLA breach confirmed (range estimate: $1k–$5k depending on window).
3) Priority engineering post-mortem and a follow-up change to admission/backpressure policy (propose: adaptive fallback earlier + graded queuing).

If approved, we’ll communicate a customer-facing RCA by tomorrow EOD. I recommend we authorize the burst capacity immediately to stop the tail from re-emerging while the team completes the root-cause.

— Stephanie
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, Katy Zhang <katy@quantaralabs.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Quantara production impact — exec summary & recommended authorizations

Action plan (timeline + rollback):
- 17:15 PT (today): Keep soft concurrency = 24 for Quantara for 2 more hours while we monitor memory and kernel fallback rates.
- 18:00 PT: Deploy an adaptive admission gate that reduces batch admission when KV miss rate > 30% (can be toggled per-customer).
- 20:00 PT: Full post-mortem draft (root cause + long-term mitigations) and customer-friendly RCA.
- Rollback: If memory OOMs or kernel fallbacks > 2%/min, revert concurrency to 16 and route 20% to hosted model until fix.

Deliverables: mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook + runbooks attached), prioritized JIRA EPIC: INF-2042 (adaptive-admission), proposed public statement draft for Quantara.

Markus
Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Attachments: mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf (pdf)
